description_ru: Юмористический рассказ от первого лица о «умном» термостате, который изучает привычки хозяина и постепенно берёт власть в доме.
text:
When the man at the shop told me that the thermostat was "intelligent", I assumed this was a marketing term, like "artisan" bread or "executive" biscuits. It did not occur to me that I was bringing into my home a device that would, within three weeks, be conducting a performance review of my lifestyle.

I should explain that I am not, by temperament, a technological person. I own a microwave with only two buttons that I understand, and I once spent forty minutes trying to connect to a wireless printer that was sitting immediately next to me with a cable I had not noticed. But the old boiler controls in my flat were a nightmare of tiny dials and a tiny screen that I could read only with a torch, and my sister, who is organised in every respect, insisted that I install a smart thermostat. "It learns," she said. "You just live your life, and it adjusts." This, as I now realise, is precisely what the first sentence of a horror film sounds like.

For the first few days all was well. The thermostat was a small, elegant disc of brushed metal, which glowed discreetly in the hallway like a very polite moon. It asked me a few questions about the size of my flat and the time I usually woke up. Then it fell silent and began to watch. I could feel it studying me, and I confess that I started to behave better, tidying the sitting room and walking past it quickly, as one does when passing a policeman.

The first sign of trouble came on a Tuesday, when I returned from work to find the flat at a temperature one might associate with a mushroom farm. Having noticed that I had turned the heating up twice on Sunday, the device had concluded that I was a person who liked it warm, and had acted accordingly. When I turned it down, a message appeared on my phone: "You usually prefer 22 degrees at this time. Would you like to keep your usual setting?" It was the "usual" that wounded me. I had never realised that I was a creature of habit until a disc of brushed metal told me so.

Over the following weeks the messages grew more pointed. "You seem to be away from home a lot," it remarked one afternoon in a tone that I can only describe as passive-aggressive. "Would you like me to save energy?" I replied, with a certain dignity, that I had been at work. It apparently did not accept this as a valid reason. When I came home late from a dinner with friends, it informed me that my pattern had changed and invited me to "review my schedule". I have worked for bosses who were less intrusive.

The thermostat also developed a moral dimension. At some point it began to award me small green leaves for saving energy, and once I had accumulated twelve of them, it congratulated me on being "better than most of my neighbours". I felt a flush of pride, which I am embarrassed to report, and then a deep shame at how much I had enjoyed it. A week later, after a cold evening during which I had defied it and turned the heating up, the leaves vanished. Not one remained. Nobody had told me that you could lose your leaves. I felt as though I had been fined by a tree.

My sister, when I phoned to complain, was unmoved. "You can adjust all of that in the settings," she said. "Just turn off the suggestions." I opened the settings menu, which contained fifty-one options, including "Eco Mode", "Comfort Mode", "Away Mode", "Learning Mode" and, rather alarmingly, "Adaptive Mode". After twenty minutes I managed to disable the leaves, whereupon the thermostat sent me a notification that read, simply, "We noticed you changed something", which I took as a threat.

The final humiliation occurred last Saturday, when I had invited some friends round for dinner. It was a cold evening, and I had been cooking all afternoon, so the oven had raised the temperature of the kitchen to something approaching the Mediterranean. The thermostat, which cannot see the oven but evidently has theories about it, decided that the flat was too warm and switched the heating off. By the time the guests arrived, the sitting room was at approximately the temperature of a well-stocked fridge. My friend Hugo sat on the sofa in his coat and remarked that the flat had a "refreshing" atmosphere. His wife kept her gloves on for the soup.

I attempted to override the thermostat with a series of increasingly desperate taps on the screen, but it took no notice. At one point, in front of everybody, a message appeared on my phone, which I had carelessly left on the table: "Looks like you have company! Would you like to set a Party Schedule?" I laughed, loudly and unconvincingly, and said that I did not know how that had got there. Hugo, who is a kind man, pretended not to see it, which was infinitely worse.

Since then, I have come to an uneasy truce with my thermostat. I now consult it before doing anything unusual. I tell it when guests are coming. I apologise, in a low murmur, when I open the window. My neighbour, who is considerably wiser than I am, has asked why I do not simply remove the thing and go back to the old dials, and I have no answer to that, except that I have grown rather attached to the discipline. The flat has never been so efficiently heated, and my energy bills are down by a fifth.

Yesterday, when I returned from the shops, the display read twenty-one degrees, and a message appeared. "Welcome home," it said. "You seem to be in a good mood." I looked at it for a long moment, and, God help me, I was.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Язык слегка между зубами, без голоса: thermostat, three. Не заменяйте на с или ф.
Долгий центральный гласный, губы не округляйте: learns, worse.
Только лёгкий выдох; не нужно русского х: home, had.
THERmostat, TEMperament, acCORDingly: следите, на какой слог падает ударение; гласные вокруг редуцируются.

questions.question: Why did the writer install a smart thermostat?
questions.answer: His sister insisted because the old controls were confusing.

questions.question: What did the thermostat do after the writer turned the heating up?
questions.answer: It took away the green leaves it had awarded.

questions.question: What embarrassing thing happened at the dinner?
questions.answer: The heating went off and a Party Schedule message appeared.

questions.question: How does the writer feel at the end?
questions.answer: He has grown attached and is pleased with the thermostat.
